title: Clopen restriction to a proper henselian closed fibre
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let f:Y → Spec A be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let i:Y₀ → Y be the closed fibre in a cartesian square over Spec(A/I) → Spec A. For clopen U,V ⊆ Y, equality i⁻¹(U)=i⁻¹(V) implies U=V. Every clopen V ⊆ Y₀ equals i⁻¹(U) for a clopen U ⊆ Y.

source.place: Lemma 59.91.1, Tag 0A0B, applied to locally constant two-valued functions

proof.text: *Step 1 (the closed fibre as a closed subset).* $S_0\to S$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], hence so is its base change $i:Z_0=Z\times_SS_0\to Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. By definition of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i$ is a homeomorphism of $Z_0$ onto the closed subset $T=i(Z_0)\subseteq Z$. For an open $W\subseteq Z$, the scheme $W\times_SS_0=W\times_ZZ_0$ is the open subscheme $i^{-1}(W)$ of $Z_0$. Since $i:Z_0\to T$ is a homeomorphism, $W'\mapsto i(W')$ is a bijection from the open and closed subsets of $Z_0$ to the open and closed subsets of $T$ (relative topology), and it sends $i^{-1}(W)$ to $W\cap T$.

source.place: Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B), statement: $Z=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ as a closed subset; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 (Tag 0A0B applied to the sheaf of $\{0,1\}$-valued locally constant functions).* Let $\mathcal C$ be the sheaf on the topological space $Z$ with $\mathcal C(U)$ the set of continuous maps $U\to\{0,1\}$ ($\{0,1\}$ discrete); $\chi\mapsto\chi^{-1}(1)$ identifies $\mathcal C(U)$ with the set of open and closed subsets of $U$, compatibly with restriction ($U'\subseteq U$: $\chi^{-1}(1)\cap U'$). Its inverse image $\mathcal C|_T$ along $T\subseteq Z$ has $\Gamma(T,\mathcal C|_T)$ = continuous maps $T\to\{0,1\}$, the restriction map $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal C)\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal C|_T)$ being $\chi\mapsto\chi|_T$: a section of the inverse image is, near each point $t\in T$, the restriction to $T$ of a section $\chi$ of $\mathcal C$ over an open $V\ni t$ of $Z$, hence locally constant on $T$, and germs at $t$ are determined by their values near $t$; conversely a continuous $\chi:T\to\{0,1\}$ is locally constant, so near each $t\in T$ it is the restriction of the constant function $\chi(t)$ on an open of $Z$, and these local sections of the presheaf inverse image agree on overlaps and glue in the sheafification. The lemma [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-h0-proper-henselian-pair] for the henselian pair $(A,I)$, the proper $Z\to S$ and the sheaf $\mathcal C$ says that $\chi\mapsto\chi|_T$ is bijective; that is, $W\mapsto W\cap T$ is a bijection from the open and closed subsets of $Z$ to those of $T$.

source.place: Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag 0A0B), label lemma-zariski-h0-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 18167; the choice of the sheaf $\mathcal C$ and the computation of $\Gamma(T,\mathcal C|_T)$ written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 3 (statement (a)).* By Steps 1 and 2, $W\mapsto i^{-1}(W)=W\times_SS_0$ is the composite of the bijection $W\mapsto W\cap T$ (Step 2) and the inverse of the bijection $W'\mapsto i(W')$ (Step 1), hence a bijection from the open and closed subsets of $Z$ to those of $Z_0$. If $W$ is open and closed with $W\times_SS_0=\emptyset$, then $W$ and $\emptyset$ have the same image, so $W=\emptyset$ by injectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.henselian_clopen_restriction
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I]
    {Y Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] (i : Y₀ ⟶ Y)
    (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ Spec (.of (A ⧸ I)))
    (h : IsPullback i f₀ f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))) :
    (∀ U V : Set Y, IsOpen U ∧ IsClosed U → IsOpen V ∧ IsClosed V →
      i.base ⁻¹' U = i.base ⁻¹' V → U = V) ∧
    (∀ V : Set Y₀, IsOpen V ∧ IsClosed V →
      ∃ U : Set Y, (IsOpen U ∧ IsClosed U) ∧ i.base ⁻¹' U = V)
